newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rise capped by origins.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rise capped by origins.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures started Wednesday on a high note on trade and industry buying but prices pulled back from the peaks by midsession on renewed origin offers.
Benchmark September opened $35 higher at $1,820 and then motored to the high at $1,835.
But it soon lost its steam, finishing midday just $27 up at $1,812, on overhead origin selling.
Volume at 2,085 lots was meagre and dominated by the September position.
Technically, analysts said the market was likely to continue base-building following the recent sharp downward move, before attempting another rally.

Susan Rigg, an analyst at Chart Analysis, said coffee continued to hold above boundaries of support. On the upside, the $2,000 level basis September was seen more as a psychological barrier than anything else.
The last time the contract held above $2,000 was on June 10 and well below the twin peaks of $2,700 in late May.
New York arabica futures ended Tuesday higher, bolstered by speculative buying amid an USDA attache report for the 1997/98 Brazil crop.

The attache report, dated May 9, put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million 60-kg bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June.
